questions.stem: Which selector has the highest specificity?
questions.explanation: #nav ul li is (0,1,0,2). All others have 0 IDs. A single ID beats any number of classes/elements.

questions.stem: With box-sizing: border-box, a div with width: 200px, padding: 20px, border: 5px has a rendered outer width of:
questions.explanation: border-box includes padding and border inside the declared width. With content-box the same element would be 200 + 40 + 10 = 250px.

questions.stem: In flexbox with flex-direction: column, justify-content controls:
choices: Vertical alignment of items (the main axis)
Spacing between rows of wrapped items
questions.explanation: justify-content is always on the main axis. When flex-direction is column, the main axis is vertical.

questions.stem: Which element is removed from normal document flow?
questions.explanation: absolute and fixed remove the element from flow. relative keeps it in flow (just offsets visually); sticky behaves like relative until its threshold.
body #x.note is (0,1,1,1) which beats (0,1,0,0). Higher specificity wins regardless of source order.

questions.stem: What does `grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr 1fr` produce?
questions.explanation: fr is a fractional unit dividing remaining space. The ratio 1:2:1 gives 25/50/25 percent.

questions.stem: Which is the correct semantic element for the main navigation?
questions.explanation: <nav> is the HTML5 semantic element for navigation blocks. It improves accessibility and SEO.

questions.stem: An element has position: absolute but no positioned ancestor. Where is it positioned relative to?
choices: The initial containing block (effectively the html element)
questions.explanation: Absolute positioning bubbles up looking for the nearest non-static ancestor. With none, it falls back to the initial containing block.

questions.stem: Which is true about !important?
choices: It can only be used in inline styles
It elevates a declaration above all non-important declarations regardless of specificity
It makes a selector more specific
It is only respected by older browsers
questions.explanation: !important changes the cascade tier so the declaration outranks any non-important rule, even one with much higher specificity.

questions.stem: What is the specificity of `a:hover`?
questions.explanation: Pseudo-classes count as classes. a is one element (d=1), :hover is one class (c=1) → (0,0,1,1).

questions.stem: Flexbox is best described as a:
questions.explanation: Flexbox lays out items along a single axis (row or column). Grid is the two-dimensional system.

questions.stem: Given `flex: 1 1 200px;` on an item, which is correct?
choices: It has a fixed width of 200px
It can grow and shrink with a 200px basis
It will not appear if container is < 200px
questions.explanation: The shorthand is grow shrink basis. grow=1 and shrink=1 mean it flexes both directions; 200px is the starting size.

questions.stem: Which heading structure is correct?
questions.explanation: Headings must form a tree without skipping levels. h1 → h2 → h3 then back to h2 to start a sibling section is valid.

questions.stem: Which CSS unit is relative to the root font size?
questions.explanation: rem = root em, always relative to html font-size. em is relative to the element's own font-size.

questions.stem: What does `align-items: center` do in a flex row?
choices: Centers the container in the page
questions.explanation: align-items is the cross-axis property. In a row, cross axis is vertical, so items are centered vertically.

questions.stem: Margin collapsing applies to:
choices: Vertical margins of adjacent block elements in normal flow
questions.explanation: Adjacent vertical margins collapse to the larger of the two. Horizontal margins, flex/grid children, and padding never collapse.

questions.stem: Which selector matches the second list item?
questions.explanation: nth-child(2) selects the element that is the 2nd child of its parent.

questions.stem: Why use semantic HTML over a soup of divs?
choices: It improves accessibility, SEO, and code clarity
It is required by the HTML parser
questions.explanation: Semantic tags carry meaning for assistive tech and crawlers and make the document tree readable. The visual rendering is the same.

questions.stem: What does `display: inline-block` enable that `display: inline` does not?
questions.explanation: Inline elements ignore width/height. inline-block respects them while still flowing inline with surrounding text.
Despite .a.b being more specific (0,0,2,0 vs 0,0,1,0), the !important on .a moves it into a higher cascade tier.

questions.stem: What is the meaning of `gap: 1rem` in a flex container?
choices: Adds 1rem space between adjacent items only
questions.explanation: gap creates space only between items, not around the container edges. Cleaner than item margins.

questions.stem: Which is true about `<article>` vs `<section>`?
choices: <article> is for self-contained content; <section> is a thematic grouping
questions.explanation: An <article> should make sense extracted on its own (blog post, comment). <section> groups related content within a larger document.

questions.stem: Which is the cleanest way to vertically center a single child inside a container?
choices: Use position: absolute with negative margins
Use display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
Use vertical-align: middle on the parent
Use line-height equal to the container height
questions.explanation: Flexbox centering on both axes is the modern, reliable way and works regardless of child size.

questions.stem: What does `box-sizing: content-box` (the default) mean for a div with width: 100px, padding: 10px?
choices: The width is overridden to fit content
questions.explanation: content-box adds padding outside the declared width. 100 + 10 + 10 = 120px rendered.

questions.stem: What problem does `<label for="email">Email</label><input id="email">` solve?
choices: Associates the label with the input for screen readers and click-to-focus
questions.explanation: The for/id pairing makes the label clickable to focus the field and exposes the relationship to assistive technology.
